RSI on the full history: S&P to 1928, Nasdaq, VIX, oil, gold and the rest

Statistics · 28 Sep 2026 · built 2026-09-28 13:19 UTC · RSI(14), Wilder, daily closes · data to 2026-09-25 · research, not rules · nothing here predicts
STATUS · every table below is computed from real daily bars; 17 instruments. Green means up, red means down. A share (“higher”) is green when it beats the same share on any day and red when it falls short. “Middle result” is the median: half the cases did better, half worse. The “90% range” shows how sure the middle result is; if the any-day number sits inside that range, the difference may be luck.

The answers you asked for

  1. SPY's bottom 10% is an RSI of 39.5 or lower (2003–2026). SPY enters it about 4.6 times a year and usually stays 6 sessions (a quarter of the visits last 11.0+; the longest 25). The longer S&P 500 index record (1928–2026) says the same: bottom 10% = 36.4 or lower, 3.8 visits a year, 5 sessions typical.
  2. What SPY did next (from the close of the first day in the zone, 105 visits): 20 sessions later the middle result was +2.0% against +1.3% on any day, and it was higher 66.7% of the time against 65.7%. After 60 sessions: +3.5% against +3.3%. On the long S&P index record the edge is smaller: +1.4% against +1.0% at 20 sessions, and +2.3% against +2.4% at 60 — no better than any day.
  3. It usually gets a little worse first. In the 20 sessions after SPY enters its bottom 10%, the lowest close was typically -1.9% below the entry (any day: -1.5%). Entering the zone is a place to start watching, not a low.
  4. Does the Nasdaq go deeper than the S&P in RSI terms? No — not over the full history either. Nasdaq 100 vs S&P 500 on the same days, 1985–2026: bottom 1% 27.6 vs 28.5, bottom 5% 34.5 vs 34.9, bottom 10% 38.6 vs 39.1 — the same floor. At the S&P's 48 falls of 10%+, the Nasdaq 100's lowest RSI nearby went below the S&P's only 15 times. Where the Nasdaq differs is the TOP: its top 5% is 73.6 vs 72.1 (it runs hotter, it does not sink deeper). QQQ vs SPY since 2011 agrees (bottom 5% 36.1 vs 35.7). The broad Nasdaq Composite is the exception: it does read lower (bottom 5% 30.1 vs 33.4), all of it from before 2003 (the 1970s–80s record and the dot-com years); since 2003 the Composite and the S&P read the same.
  5. RSI divergence is rare at true pivots and, so far, not an edge on the S&P. A bullish divergence (price lower low, RSI higher low, confirmed 10 sessions after the low) appeared 11 times on SPY in 23 years and 64 times on the S&P index since 1928. After it, the S&P index did +1.2% in 20 sessions — against +1.4% after lower lows WITHOUT a divergence. Bearish divergence did not mark tops: the S&P rose +1.7% in the next 20 sessions after one. Small samples; section 4 has every instrument.
  6. Where everything sits today (close of 2026-09-25, against each one's own full history). Low: TLT (long Treasuries fund) 31.6 (bottom 4.2%), IWM (Russell 2000 fund) 34.9 (bottom 5.7%), Russell 2000 index 34.9 (bottom 8.1%), DIA (Dow fund) 43.1 (bottom 17.5%), Dow Jones Industrial 43.6 (bottom 18.6%). High: US dollar index 67.2 (top 9.8%), US 10-year yield 75.3 (top 4.5%). Small caps are in their bottom 10% while the Nasdaq 100 is in its top 21.3%.

4 · RSI divergence at confirmed pivots

Bullish divergence: price makes a swing low below the previous swing low (within 60 sessions), but RSI at the new low is higher than at the old one. Bearish: price makes a higher swing high while RSI makes a lower one. A swing low is only known 10 sessions later (it needs 10 higher lows on each side), so every result starts from the close on that confirmation day, and “price already moved by confirmation” shows how far price had bounced (or fell) from the pivot by then. The comparison that matters is the next column pair: the same kind of pivot WITHOUT a divergence.

7 · How this was done, and what could be wrong

RSI
RSI(14) with Wilder's smoothing on daily closes (the same arithmetic the Hub and the S7–S9 studies use, research/statistics/stats.mjs). The first 14 sessions of each history have no RSI.
Where the prices come from
SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, TLT: the chart API's daily bars (Massive), split-adjusted, 2003 on. VIX, oil (WTI), gold, silver, Bitcoin, the dollar index and the 10-year yield: the chart API's full FMP history. S&P 500 index (1928 on), Nasdaq 100 (1985 on), Nasdaq Composite (1971 on), Russell 2000 (1987 on), Dow (1985 on): FMP's index history, fetched on 28 Sep from inside the Fly bar-service machine (the key never left Fly). All saved outside the repo in stats-cache/daily-bars-rsi/.
Pivots and swings
S9's rule: a swing low has a low below the 10 bars before it and at or below the 10 after it (a high mirrors it). Section 6's swing tables use the S9 swings (alternating, each end moved to the true extreme), which is descriptive. Section 4 uses only raw confirmed pivots and acts 10 sessions later — no look-ahead. A 5/5 window is shown as a check.
The 90% range
Month-clustered bootstrap: the visits are grouped by the calendar month they started in, whole months are drawn at random with replacement 2,000 times (fixed seed), and the middle result is recomputed each time. The range is the 5th to 95th of those. It is shown for the signal only; the any-day number rests on thousands of days and is treated as fixed.
What could be wrong
  • Hindsight in the lines. The bottom-10% and top-10% lines are set from the full history. The no-hindsight check (end of section 3) is the honest version; its edges are smaller.
  • Overlap. 60-session results from visits a month apart share most of their days, so they are not independent. The month clustering handles part of that, not all; treat 60-session ranges as too narrow.
  • Old data. Before about 1983 the S&P index (and before 1985 the Composite) has closes only, no highs or lows; RSI is fine (it uses closes) but early pivots are close-based. The Nasdaq Composite's lower RSI floor comes from before 2003: at the S&P's 10%+ falls before 1985 the Composite went deeper 18 times out of 20, and since 2003 the two floors match.
  • Bad prints. 16 impossible wicks were clamped to the bar's body (the 14 S9 listed plus oil's negative April 2020 low): SPY 2004-03-16 (low 11.7 against a close of 111.79); SPY 2004-08-18 (high 1107.07 against a close of 110.03); SPY 2004-12-21 (low 52.67 against a close of 120.39); SPY 2005-02-17 (high 170.76 against a close of 120.23); SPY 2005-05-27 (high 1120.2 against a close of 120.25); SPY 2006-01-26 (low 57.29 against a close of 127.36); SPY 2008-09-29 (low 11.85 against a close of 111.38); SPY 2008-11-07 (low 53.15 against a close of 93.86); QQQ 2003-09-24 (high 43.8 against a close of 33.22); QQQ 2004-07-28 (low 0 against a close of 34.38); IWM 2004-07-30 (high 5486.5 against a close of 55); IWM 2008-09-19 (high 152.01 against a close of 75.01); IWM 2009-06-16 (high 512.7 against a close of 50.5); CLUSD 2020-04-20 (low -40.32 against a close of 17.73); CLUSD 2020-04-21 (low+high -16.74 against a close of 10.01); BTCUSD 2013-04-12 (low 54.25 against a close of 117). VIX is exempt: its 50%+ intraday spikes are real (5 Aug 2024). One VIX low (10 Oct 2008, 28.13) looks wrong but is left as served; it only affects VIX pivots, not RSI.
  • QQQ's hole. The chart API has no QQQ bars from Dec 2004 to Mar 2011, so QQQ starts in 2011; the Nasdaq 100 index covers 1985 on.
  • Weekend prints. The chart API serves Sunday bars for the dollar, oil, gold and silver since late 2024 (extra bars on days with no session). They were dropped here; the Station may still draw them.
  • Prices only. No dividends. Oil is FMP's continuous front contract (roll jumps included).
  • Small samples. Divergences at 10/10 pivots are rare (a handful a year at most); read the 90% range before the middle result.
What was not done
  • No buy or sell rule is proposed. Nothing here is back-tested as a strategy.
  • Hidden divergence (price higher low, RSI lower low) and divergence on weekly bars were not measured.
  • Weighting by recency or market cap (Alan's 27 Sep note) is not applied; every year counts the same.
  • Pre-1928 S&P, put/call, CNN Fear & Greed and VIX term structure are not in this study.
  • No database write, no deploy. The page is on the branch for the coordinator.
Files
research/statistics/rsi-history.mjs (the engine), research/statistics/rsi-history-page.mjs (this page), tests/statistics-rsi-history.test.mjs, and the full numbers in rsi-full-history.json next to this page.
